reason:
Verified from the CDP accessibility tree (Accessibility.getFullAXTree), not innerText, on BOTH grounds and all three guest states. The DisclosureTriangle name is 'BEHIND YOU 3 moments +' closed and 'BEHIND YOU 3 moments −' open on paper/phone, paper/desk, ink/phone, ink/desk; 'BEHIND YOU 9 moments +' / '−' on paper/day and ink/day. The name sources array shows type='contents' carrying the mark, with aria-labelledby and aria-label both empty, so the pseudo-element is the sole reason the character is in the name. innerText is 'BEHIND YOU
3 moments' in every case, so the mark reaches the tree and nothing else. The redundancy is real: the same node already exposes expanded=false/true as a property, so the mark restates the state a second time in a grammar no screen reader will phrase ('plus' / 'minus'). b.css:432 and b.css:440 are the ONLY two non-empty string content declarations in the whole stylesheet (grep 'content: "' returns exactly those two lines) — every other presentational mark is drawn or aria-hidden, so the finding's 'only place a decorative mark reaches the tree' claim holds. Not in SETTLED.md (57 ids checked; nothing on the summary's name or on generated content). Not a gate restatement: interaction-check.mjs:1450-1466 asserts only that the ::after computed content is not 'none' and differs between closed and open — it never reads the accessible name. The proposed fix is implementable and I drove it: injecting `content: "+" / ""` and `content: "−" / ""` drops the mark from the name in all eight variant/state/open combinations while leaving the painted glyph byte-identical — element screenshots of .b-behindSummary hash-match the unpatched build in all eight (paper/ink × phone/day × closed/open), computed ::after width stays 8.375px, font Geist Mono, size 11px, colour unchanged, summary box 364×44 unchanged, and the existing gate assertion still passes because the computed content strings remain distinct and non-'none'. No constraint is touched: no colour, no weight, no structure. Two minor wrinkles in the write-up, neither load-bearing: (a) the finding cites render-core.js micro() as evidence uppercase is kept out of the tree — the comment says so, but Chromium applies text-transform when computing name-from-contents, which is why the measured name is 'BEHIND YOU', not 'Behind you'; (b) the proposed assertion, as literally worded, would fail for that same reason, since .b-behindLabel textContent is 'Behind you'. Both are fixed in the sharpened form below.
sharpenedFix: Ship the alt-text form, but declare the plain value first so an engine without alternative-text support keeps the glyph rather than dropping the whole declaration and losing the open/closed mark (which would also fail interaction-check.mjs's 'the door says whether it is open'). b.css:431-440 becomes `.b-behindSummary::after { content: "+"; content: "+" / ""; ... }` and `.b-behindDetails[open] .b-behindSummary::after { content: "2"; content: "2" / ""; }`. Driven at 390 on paper/phone this yields name 'BEHIND YOU 3 moments' closed AND open, computed content '"+" / ""' → '"−" / ""' (still distinct, still not 'none'), height 44 — so the existing gate is untouched. For the new assertion, compare against the UPPERCASED label: in interaction-check.mjs, for states phone, desk and day on both grounds, read the summary's accessible name via a CDP Accessibility.getFullAXTree lookup (getComputedStyle cannot see it) and require it to equal `label.textContent.toUpperCase() + ' ' + count.textContent` — asserting on the raw textContent would fail on the text-transform, not on the defect.
